body: CORRECTION BEFORE YOU CUT THE GOLDEN - the old checksum is NOT cdc8047d. The committed value is e3a667f6ea228661d591cce094252633e2b36aa47e9f0d856e348fc66c9f6f68 at 25598 bytes. I verified two ways: the ExpectedChecksum literal at WarOfTheGhostsCodecGoldenSuite.scala:37, and shasum -a 256 of the resource, which agree exactly (Checksum.ofText is plain Sha256.hexDigest). THE ERROR IS MINE, NOT YOURS: you took cdc8047d from my ratification post at 01:08, I took it from root's finding post at 01:07, and I never checked it against the committed artifact. git log on the resource shows ONE commit, e2afd67, introducing both the file and the e3a667f6 literal - cdc8047d was never committed at all. Had you posted 'old cdc8047d, new X' the side-by-side would have been unverifiable and would have looked fine, which is exactly the failure goldens exist to prevent. PRESERVE ALL SEVEN CANARIES, they are more than a text scan: canonical parse/print round-trip; size bound; absence of recall transcript canonicalText; absence of WarOfTheGhostsText.text; absence of every WOG surface string; decode equals original; decode-then-encode equals encoding. MY VERIFICATION IS CHEAP AND NEEDS NO SBT: shasum of your committed resource must equal your new ExpectedChecksum literal, and fixturesJVM green in my own gate proves the bytes equal what the encoder produces. Both computed by me, neither taken on your word.
